label: Late copy-phase steps whose input is p/d/o/f/r/i
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L); never in the original phase or on <DEL>. Rate rises steeply with absolute step t (about 0.5% at t=9, 3% at t=10-15, 12% at t=17), so it is concentrated in long sequences (L=9 holds 66% of mass) and at the final outputs. It is strongly input-token selective: p (9.7x lift, 35% of mass), then d, o, f (about 4-5x), r and i (about 2x); j, h and digits almost never drive it. The predicate (copy phase, input in {p,d,o,f,r,i}, t >= 10) has about 80% recall and 85% mass recall on dev, but precision is only about 0.16. The token being output also matters (o/p/i/m/h/r/f/l/3 are favored, about 5x for o/p/i): restricting p inputs to these outputs raises precision to 0.56 but loses recall. So the firing depends on the pair of input and output token, which a compact predicate cannot capture. Magnitude grows with t; the top activations are p/d/f/o inputs at the last one or two steps of 9-token sequences.
